fields.label: Cards ×4
rows: It has to fit before it can seal

A grommet is seated by hand over a cut panel edge. We specify hardness and tear strength for that moment, not just for service life — a part the operator has to force is a part that gets damaged on the line.
Each hole is moulded undersize against its wire. Send the wire diameters and we will set the interference — matching hole to wire exactly gives a grommet that passes inspection and leaks in service.
Sized to your panel, not to a catalogue
Panel gauge sets the retaining groove; hole pitch is fixed by your harness. Both are moulded in, so the part seats in one push and stays put.
Protecting the cable is half the job
The other half is the sheet-metal edge. A chafed harness is a short circuit, so the bore is moulded with a radius rather than cut, and the compound is chosen to stay flexible cold.
fields.note:

Card 01 is the argument a competitor will not make, because it is about the assembly line rather than the product, and it is where grommets actually fail commercially.

sections.title: From compound to certification
sections.chip: Correct process for once · two steps sharpened
sections.live: LIVE H2 → From Compound to Certification · six steps · “compression moulding” is right on this page

fields.label: Steps
rows: Material compounding — polymer blending, additive integration and batch QC in our in-house lab. Tear strength is set here — the grommet is stretched over a cut panel edge by hand, and that moment decides line scrap.
Mould design and CNC tool manufacture, in-house, held as a controlled record. The retaining groove and the three cores are cut to your panel gauge and hole pitch.
Compression moulding — [no change; correct on this part]
Post-cure and deflashing — flash removed from the three bores and the groove. Flash left in a bore is a leak path and a chafe point.
Quality inspection — hole diameters, pitch and groove dimension checked against the drawing, plus hardness testing and batch sampling.
Export packaging — industrial packing with documentation. ISPM-15 treated pallets where timber packaging is used. Grommets are bagged loose so the sealing lips are not deformed in transit.
fields.note:
Six steps, six kept, and for the first time in four sheets the process named is the process used.
Step 04 is the one worth the extra clause. Deflashing a bore is the quality difference between a grommet that seals and one that cuts into the cable it was fitted to protect, and it is invisible on a datasheet

notes: The process block must render from the part record — it happens to be right here, which is not the same as being data-driven.
Numbered steps are an <ol>.
